questions.question: What should you do if something goes wrong during a performance for the examiner? Why is this important?

points.text: Stay in character and adapt — never break character or apologise. The examiner wants to see how you handle the unexpected. A covered mistake shows professionalism; a broken character shows immaturity. Adapt and carry on.

questions.question: Describe how you would prepare for a visiting examiner assessment from one week before to the performance day.

points.text: One week before: full run-throughs with notes. Three days before: technical and dress rehearsals. Day before: light rehearsal, rest, prepare costume. Day of: warm-up, focus, silence backstage, full commitment from the first moment.

questions.question: How are individual performers assessed within a group performance? What does the examiner look for?

points.text: Each performer is marked individually on: vocal skills, physical skills, characterisation, interaction with others, and overall dramatic effectiveness. The group context matters but your personal choices, commitment and truthfulness earn your marks.
